name: Sunday Times cryptic crossword, Penguin book 2 No 76

clue.text: Doctor takes an age to go round a hill with this vehicle!
He has a way with him, it’s said
Sort Clara out or you’ll get some florid vocal passages!
Positive poet laureate to you and me
Right kind of shares for food
Best-known of the Dodgers?
Cured Sarah and Edward
Political group based on Plato’s work goes to an entertain- ing occasion
Reluctant to compose a poem
Divides continually on board
Spasmodic attacks made here in Rome by vessels
Escape from error
Commonly frightened by the rush for payment in the enclosure
Voice in trouble a lot
Part-district of a Durham town
Ata former time shut up in a dungeon cell
Pictures of greasy liquids?
Automobile taken north by a learner bodily!
Wrestling with an instruction to the fielders?
‘—., like straws upon the surface flow’ (Dryden: Prologues — and Epilovues)
Exclusive seers? Out of sight!
Unlucky — yet perhaps it’s all right quickly to get the danger signal
Dealt pies and, one hears, tea out as basic food
“Not one life shall be destroy’d, Or cast as — to the void’ (Tennyson: In Memoriam)
Specimens should be large enough in the liner
High-flier ?
Crews from the East — a strange sight
All-rounder offers final odds on the spot!
Not written past this like a shepherd
Immediately gets a refusal abroad
